attributes.description: Write mode: append, overwrite, error (alias errorifexists) or ignore

Template on a connection string. Template is: '{dialect}{jdbc_host}:{jdbc_port}/{jdbc_database}', manually replace the following values: {jdbc_host}, {jdbc_port}, {jdbc_database} and {dialect}, current supported {dialect} options are 'jdbc:oracle:thin:@', 'jdbc:postgresql://', 'jdbc:mysql://', 'jdbc:redshift://', redshift does not support extraction of columns information. Databricks jobs do support having ':' between port and database - '{jdbc_port}:{jdbc_database}', this is not supported for Glue jobs.

A driver class name to use. For instance: oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver. Not needed for drivers based on JDBC 4.0 and above (auto load feature). This software also supports various other JDBC drivers including but not limited to: PostgreSQL (org.postgresql.Driver), Amazon Redshift (com.amazon.redshift.jdbc42.Driver), Presto (io.prestosql.jdbc.PrestoDriver), Microsoft SQL Server (com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver), MySQL (com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver), OSIsoft (com.osisoft.jdbc.Driver), and SAP HANA (com.sap.db.jdbc.Driver).
A custom format can be configured in order to properly handle various data types
Spark jdbc write options. For complete list of options see https://spark.apache.org/docs/3.1.1/api/python/reference/api/pyspark.sql.DataFrameWriter.jdbc.html
